linear_regression.name: Linear Regression
linear_regression.strength: Log-price linear elasticity with fast inference and direct coefficient interpretation
linear_regression.challenge: Cannot capture higher-order non-linear spatial interactions

decision_tree.name: Decision Tree Regression
decision_tree.strength: Captures non-linear feature thresholds and interactions with explicit decision rules
decision_tree.challenge: Higher variance than ensemble tree methods

random_forest.name: Random Forest Regression
random_forest.strength: Variance reduction via bootstrap aggregation of deep regression trees in log-price space
random_forest.challenge: Larger memory footprint and slower inference than gradient boosting

xgboost.name: XGBoost Regression
xgboost.strength: Highest accuracy via log-target gradient boosting, L1/L2 regularization &RandomizedSearchCV
xgboost.challenge: Requires TreeSHAP explainability and conformal calibration for intervals

conformal_intervals.method: Split Conformal Prediction (Dwelling-Type Stratified Log-Residual Quantiles on Out-of-Fold Calibration Set)
conformal_intervals.formula: [exp(log(1 + y_hat) - q_{1-alpha, type}) - 1, exp(log(1 + y_hat) + q_{1-alpha, type}) - 1]

residual_analysis.key_finding: Empirical Holdout Residual Finding: Absolute dollar errors exhibit heteroscedasticity across price tiers — Holdout MAE increases from $66,536 (MAPE 14.68%) for properties Under $600k and $96,365 (MAPE 12.16%) in the $600k–$1.0M core market to $679,815 (MAPE 20.27%, mean residual +$620,501) for luxury properties Over $2.5M (n = 151), where unrecorded architectural prestige, renovation quality, and view lines drive bespoke variance. Across dwelling types, Units/Apartments (u) achieve the lowest dollar MAE ($99,300, MAPE 14.95%), whereas detached Houses (h) have a higher dollar MAE ($162,389, MAPE 12.95%) due to land-value dispersion.
